sources.name: Launch (The Intelligence Company's launch-closure program): its place check on Orbit's own hazard areas and scheduled launches
sources.licence: The suite's own program, published openly (launch.theintelligence.company/data/snapshot.json). Orbit uses only Launch's match rows on Orbit's areas: the level (time and place, grouped, time), azimuth, distance and implied inclination. Each underlying item keeps its source's terms (NGA, Launch Library 2, GCAT).
sources.note: orbit-2.10 (Tom's 'do all four', 16 Nov 2026): one request a run. Grade is Orbit's call: Launch's method is published and tested (B); a place match is a geometric coincidence with its pad's closure history, not a confirmation that an area is for a launch (2).

sources.name: Launch Library 2, The Space Devs: upcoming launches, and every launch since 1 Jan 2024 (Orbit's ledger)
sources.licence: Free access to the whole database ("the entire database is accessible to everyone, for free", thespacedevs.com/llapi, read 16 Nov 2026), 15 requests an hour without a key. No separate data licence is stated; Tom, 15 Nov 2026: freely available, so Orbit uses and republishes it with credit (the ledger on Orbit's public release). Images not used: each carries its own licence.

sources.name: Spaceflight News API (Spaceflight News API and The Space Devs): headlines tied to Launch Library 2 launches
sources.licence: No licence, terms of use or rate limit stated (site read 15 Nov 2026; footer 'Copyright © 2026 Spaceflight News API & The Space Devs'). Orbit keeps links only: headline, outlet, time and the link to the outlet's page; no summaries, no images. Asked in Tom's email to The Space Devs (15 Nov 2026).
sources.note: orbit-2.5 (Tom's 'Yes, links only', 15 Nov 2026): one request a run, filtered to the scheduled launches' Launch Library 2 ids. Grade is Orbit's call: the API usually links the right launch (B); the headlines are the outlets' own reporting, not checked (3).

sources.name: NGA Maritime Safety Information: in-force daily memoranda for HYDROPAC, HYDROLANT, HYDROARC, NAVAREA IV and NAVAREA XII (launch hazard and space-debris warnings)
sources.licence: US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105). NGA's own terms page could not be read: the MSI portal and API answer 503 'under maintenance' (since at least 6 Nov 2026); the memoranda are served from that maintenance page. The memoranda say they supplement, and do not replace, IMO/SOLAS broadcasts (read 13 Nov 2026).
sources.note: Official coordinator for NAVAREA IV and XII; HYDROPAC/HYDROLANT/HYDROARC rebroadcast other coordinators' warnings. Read the MSI API (broadcast-warn) when it returns.

sources.name: Japan Coast Guard, Hydrographic and Oceanographic Department: NAVAREA XI navigational warnings (launch hazard and space-debris warnings)
sources.licence: Government of Japan Standard Terms of Use 2.0 (www1.kaiho.mlit.go.jp/copyright.html, read 13 Nov 2026): reuse, including commercial, with the source credited and edits marked; not to be presented as the government's own. Article 25 of the Hydrographic Services Act (publications similar to charts and nautical publications need permission) is not read as covering warnings; unverified.
sources.note: NAVAREA XI coordinator: western North Pacific, including waters off China. Titles Japanese, warning text English; issue times stamped JST. Not read since 14 Nov 2026: the site's robots.txt disallows /TUHO/ (where the list and messages sit) for every crawler but the National Diet Library's. Read 13-14 Nov 2026 before that was seen.

sources.name: Secure World Foundation, Global Counterspace Capabilities (2026): History of ASAT Testing in Space (Google Sheets CSV export)
sources.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 ('Global Counterspace Capabilities © 2026 by Secure World Foundation is licensed under Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International', read on the report page, which links this sheet, 13 Nov 2026); credit as 'Secure World Foundation, Global Counterspace Capabilities (2026), CC BY-NC 4.0'. Non-commercial use only.
sources.note: Sheet: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1e5GtZEzdo6xk41i2_ei3c8jRZDjvP4Xwz3BVsUHwi48 (gid 0), read as CSV with no key; the sheet says 'Last Updated 17-Feb-26'. Debris counts are U.S. military catalog counts (generally 10 cm and larger), as SWF compiled them. Grade B2 confirmed by Tom, 15 Nov 2026 (the RPO sheet, if built, is graded on its own).

sources.name: Secure World Foundation, Global Counterspace Capabilities (2026): History of Robotic Rendezvous and Proximity Operations in Space (Google Sheets CSV export)
sources.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 ('is licensed under Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International', on the report page, which links this sheet under Additional Information; read 15 Nov 2026); credit as 'Secure World Foundation, Global Counterspace Capabilities (2026), CC BY-NC 4.0'. Non-commercial use only.
sources.note: Sheet: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pHzvC-zGjF34Jrd6TdmM4odTL_MinBBoS_ld9X3jsW4, tabs Commercial/Civil (gid 0), Military/Intelligence (gid 1789904048), Planned (gid 1403218889) and About (gid 1782604784, 'Last Updated 17 February 2026'), read as CSV with no key. Grade B3 is Orbit's call, graded apart from the ASAT sheet (Tom, 15 Nov 2026): the same reliable compiler, but many rows are SWF's reading of public tracking (an activity's purpose, its 'Intelligence' category, a span of months), not an operator's statement. Not in the feed.

sources.name: CelesTrak (T.S. Kelso): GP element sets, last-30-days group (the 18th Space Defense Squadron's GP data)
sources.licence: CelesTrak's usage policy (celestrak.org/usage-policy.php, read 16 Nov 2026, updated that day) states no redistribution or credit terms and asks for one download per update (GP data update every 2 hours). The sets are the 18th Space Defense Squadron's GP data, which USSPACECOM approves for redistribution as basic SSA data with citation (see space-track); credited as CelesTrak, from 18 SDS data.
sources.note: orbit-2.12 (Tom's yes, 16 Nov 2026): one request a run, for the globe's paths of recent launches' payloads only; Space-Track stays the source for watched objects and orbit changes. Same underlying data as space-track, so the same independence group. Grade is Orbit's call.

sources.name: Space-Track.org (United States Space Command, USSPACECOM, 18th Space Defense Squadron): GP and GP_HISTORY element sets
sources.licence: Account required. User Agreement (read 14 Nov 2026): no transfer of data 'including the analysis of data' 'without prior express approval'. Space-Track's documentation (read 14 Nov 2026): 'USSPACECOM has provided express blanket approval for transfer/redistribution of basic SSA data and services ... conditioned on appropriate citation', and 'Publications of analysis based on USSPACECOM data also require appropriate citations.' Credit wording: doctrine/spacetrack-disclaimer.md, approved by Tom 14 Nov 2026.
sources.note: Read for a private watch list (orbit-2.4): GP at most once an hour, off the top and bottom of the hour; each object's GP_HISTORY once only, stored in the private Actions cache. Raw element sets are not republished: the page shows changes and positions derived from them, credited as the disclaimer gives. Grade is Orbit's call, to be confirmed by Tom.
